question: Refer to the exhibit. A source is sending a multicast traffic stream to the receiver. How is the multicast traffic expected to flow through the network when it reaches a vPC peer?
context: Topology: Agg-1 (M1) and Agg-2 (M2) connect to Access-1 and Access-2 via vPC-1 and vPC-2. Source connects to Access-1 (Vlan 10), Receiver connects to Access-2 (Vlan 10). Multicast traffic stream flows from Source toward Receiver.
imageNote: Diagram: Agg-1 (M1) and Agg-2 (M2) cross-connect to Access-1 and Access-2 via vPC-1/vPC-2; Source (Vlan10) connects to Access-1, Receiver (Vlan10) connects to Access-2, multicast stream flows Source to Receiver.
options: The multicast traffic is not replicated to the ports that joined a multicast group (224.0.0.13) or the peer link. The multicast traffic stream flows over the vPC link to ensure that orphan ports get the multicast stream in failure scenarios.

The multicast traffic is replicated to the ports that joined a given multicast group and the peer link. The multicast traffic stream flows from Agg-1 to Agg-2 over the M1-to-M2 peer link and forwards the traffic over Layer 4 to Access-2.

The multicast traffic is not replicated to the ports that joined a multicast group (224.0.0.13) or the peer link. The multicast traffic stream flows from Agg-1 to Agg-2 over the M1-to-M2 peer link and forwards the traffic over Layer 4 to Access-2.
theory: The vPC peer link is always kept in a forwarding state specifically because it must carry Layer 2 multicast/IGMP-snooping state and act as a path for orphan ports — single-homed, non-vPC ports — to still receive multicast traffic even if their local vPC peer isn't the one that originally received it from the source. Multicast traffic entering one vPC peer is replicated both to local receiver ports that joined the group and across the peer link, ensuring orphan-port receivers connected to the other switch aren't left without the stream during forwarding-path changes or failures. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 2 — vPC Peer Link Multicast Forwarding and Orphan Ports)
